## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the measurement of soil pH and electrical
conductivity (EC, as a proxy for salinity) on soil-water and
soil-CaCl~2~ extracts. Soil pH controls nutrient availability, metal
solubility, microbial activity, and the fate of contaminants. Soil
salinity (estimated from EC) affects plant growth, soil structure, and
is a primary criterion for classifying saline, sodic, and saline-sodic
soils. The methods follow Thomas (1996) for pH and Rhoades (1996) for
EC, as described in the SSSA *Methods of Soil Analysis, Part 3*
[@thomas1996; @rhoades1996].

For meter operation, calibration, and electrode maintenance, see
[SOP-L300 pH and Conductivity -- Bench-Top Measurements](SOP-L300-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd).


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Air-dried, sieved (less than 2 mm) mineral soils from
  all EA Program sites; compost and potting media (with appropriate
  extraction ratios noted in Section 6)
- **Does not apply to:** In situ field pH measurements with portable
  probes (see [SOP-F200](../field_sops/SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd));
  water sample pH and conductivity (see
  [SOP-L300](SOP-L300-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd)); saturated paste
  extraction for formal salinity classification of irrigation water
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain meter and electrodes, stock reagents |
| Trained Personnel | Prepare extracts, measure and record results |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** 0.01 M CaCl~2~ is a mild irritant. pH buffer solutions
  and conductivity standards are low-hazard but should not contact eyes.
- **Physical:** No significant physical hazards beyond standard
  glassware handling.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves

### Emergency Procedures

For buffer or chemical splashes, flush with water. Refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd).


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                          | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| pH/conductivity meter         | Calibrated per [SOP-L40](SOP-L40-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd) |
| pH combination electrode      | Glass bulb with refillable KCl junction preferred |
| Conductivity cell             | With automatic temperature compensation   |
| Analytical balance (0.01 g)   | See [SOP-L13](SOP-L13-using-balances.qmd) |
| Beakers (50--100 mL)         | Clean; one per sample plus blanks         |
| Graduated cylinder or dispenser | For volumetric delivery of water or CaCl~2~ |
| Glass stirring rods           | One per sample or rinsed between samples  |
| Timer                         | For equilibration period                  |

### Reagents

| Reagent                       | Preparation / Notes                       |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Deionized water (Type I or II) | From [*SOP-L11*](SOP-L11-milli-q-water.qmd) |
| 0.01 M CaCl~2~ solution      | Dissolve 1.47 g CaCl~2~-2H~2~O in 1 L DI water |
| pH buffer solutions (4.01, 7.00, 10.01) | For pH meter calibration    |
| Conductivity standard (1413 uS/cm) | For conductivity meter calibration  |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Sample Preparation

1. Air-dry the soil at room temperature until constant mass (typically
   24--48 hours)
2. Pass the dried soil through a 2 mm sieve. See
   [SOP-F400 Soil Sampling](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd) for
   details on sieving and homogenization.
3. Store the sieved soil in a labeled bag or container at room
   temperature

### 6.2 Selecting the Extraction Ratio

Two standard soil-to-solution ratios are used. The choice depends on
the project objectives and the need for comparability with published
data:

| Ratio     | Method                 | When to Use                        |
|:----------|:-----------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| 1:1       | 10 g soil : 10 mL water (or CaCl~2~) | Most common in agronomic soil testing; closest to field conditions |
| 1:5       | 10 g soil : 50 mL water (or CaCl~2~) | Useful for saline soils, compost, or when more extract volume is needed for subsequent analyses |

::: {.callout-note}
Soil pH measured in 0.01 M CaCl~2~ is typically 0.3--0.5 units lower
than pH measured in DI water because the salt displaces H^+^ and
Al^3+^ from exchange sites. CaCl~2~ pH is less sensitive to seasonal
variation in soil salt content and is preferred for monitoring studies
where consistency over time matters [@thomas1996]. Record the extraction
medium (water or CaCl~2~) and ratio with every result.
:::

### 6.3 Preparing the Soil Slurry (1:1 Method)

1. Weigh 10.0 g of air-dried, sieved soil into a clean beaker
2. Add 10 mL of DI water (for pH~water~ and EC) or 10 mL of 0.01 M
   CaCl~2~ (for pH~CaCl2~)
3. Stir vigorously with a glass rod for 30 seconds
4. Allow to stand for 10 minutes
5. Stir briefly again before measurement

### 6.4 Preparing the Soil Extract (1:5 Method)

1. Weigh 10.0 g of air-dried, sieved soil into a clean beaker
2. Add 50 mL of DI water (or 50 mL of 0.01 M CaCl~2~)
3. Stir vigorously for 30 seconds
4. Allow to stand for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally
5. For EC measurement on the 1:5 extract, allow the soil to settle and
   insert the conductivity cell into the clear supernatant. For pH,
   insert the electrode into the slurry while still partially suspended.

### 6.5 Measuring Electrical Conductivity

::: {.callout-important}
Always measure EC before pH on the same aliquot. The pH electrode's KCl
reference junction leaks electrolyte into the sample and will
artificially elevate the EC reading [@apha2012].
:::

1. Calibrate the conductivity meter per
   [SOP-L40](SOP-L40-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd), Section 6.3
2. Rinse the conductivity cell with DI water and blot dry
3. Insert the cell into the supernatant (1:5 method) or into the
   settled portion of the slurry (1:1 method). Tap gently to dislodge
   air bubbles.
4. Allow the reading to stabilize with automatic temperature
   compensation active
5. Record the specific conductance (uS/cm at 25 C), sample ID, and
   extraction ratio
6. Rinse the cell with DI water between samples

### 6.6 Measuring Soil pH

1. Calibrate the pH meter with a three-point calibration per
   [SOP-L40](SOP-L40-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd), Section 6.2
2. Rinse the pH electrode with DI water and blot gently
3. Insert the electrode into the slurry so that the glass bulb and
   reference junction are fully immersed. For the 1:1 method, the
   electrode should contact the settled soil.
4. Allow the reading to stabilize (typically 30--60 seconds; may take
   2--3 minutes for poorly buffered soils)
5. Record the pH value, extraction medium (water or CaCl~2~), ratio,
   and sample ID
6. Rinse the electrode with DI water between samples

### 6.7 Converting 1:5 EC to Estimated Saturated Paste EC (EC~e~)

The saturated paste extract (EC~e~) is the standard for soil salinity
classification, but the 1:5 extract is quicker to prepare. An
approximate conversion can be made using the following relationship,
though the factor varies with texture [@rhoades1996]:

$$
EC_e \approx EC_{1:5} \times f
$$

where $f$ is an empirical factor:

| Soil Texture | $f$ (approximate) |
|:-------------|:-------------------|
| Sand         | 6 -- 8             |
| Loam         | 8 -- 10            |
| Clay         | 10 -- 13           |

::: {.callout-warning}
These conversion factors are approximate and site-specific. For formal
salinity classification (e.g., land-use planning, irrigation
suitability), prepare an actual saturated paste extract per USDA
Handbook 60.
:::


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### 7.1 Interpretation of Soil pH

| pH Range     | Classification      | Agronomic Significance            |
|:-------------|:--------------------|:----------------------------------|
| Less than 4.5 | Extremely acidic   | Toxic Al^3+^ levels; few crops tolerate |
| 4.5 -- 5.5   | Strongly acidic     | Low P availability; Mo deficiency; lime recommended |
| 5.5 -- 6.5   | Moderately acidic   | Suitable for most crops; some nutrient limitations |
| 6.5 -- 7.5   | Neutral             | Optimal for most crops and nutrient availability |
| 7.5 -- 8.5   | Moderately alkaline | Common in arid soils; Fe, Mn, Zn may be limiting |
| Greater than 8.5 | Strongly alkaline | Possible sodicity; Na toxicity    |

### 7.2 Interpretation of Soil Salinity (EC~e~)

| EC~e~ (dS/m)   | Classification      | Plant Response                   |
|:----------------|:--------------------|:---------------------------------|
| 0 -- 2          | Non-saline          | No yield reduction for most crops |
| 2 -- 4          | Slightly saline     | Sensitive crops affected          |
| 4 -- 8          | Moderately saline   | Many crops affected               |
| 8 -- 16         | Strongly saline     | Only tolerant crops survive       |
| Greater than 16 | Very strongly saline | Few plants survive               |

### 7.3 Saline, Sodic, and Saline-Sodic Classification

| Class         | EC~e~ (dS/m) | SAR / ESP               | pH     |
|:--------------|:-------------|:------------------------|:-------|
| Normal        | Less than 4  | SAR less than 13 / ESP less than 15 | Variable |
| Saline        | 4 or greater | SAR less than 13 / ESP less than 15 | Usually less than 8.5 |
| Sodic         | Less than 4  | SAR 13 or greater / ESP 15 or greater | Usually greater than 8.5 |
| Saline-sodic  | 4 or greater | SAR 13 or greater / ESP 15 or greater | Variable |

SAR = sodium adsorption ratio; ESP = exchangeable sodium percentage.
Full SAR/ESP determination requires cation analysis beyond the scope of
this SOP.

### 7.4 QC Requirements

- Calibrate the pH meter before each measurement session (three-point).
  Acceptable slope: 90--102% of theoretical.
- Calibrate the conductivity meter before each session
- Re-read pH 7.00 buffer after every 10 samples; recalibrate if drift
  exceeds +/- 0.05 pH units
- Re-read the conductivity standard after every 10 samples; recalibrate
  if drift exceeds +/- 5%
- Run a DI water blank and a laboratory reference soil (if available)
  with each batch
- Run duplicate measurements on at least 10% of samples. Acceptable
  precision: +/- 0.1 pH units and +/- 5% relative percent difference
  for EC.
- Record extraction medium, ratio, calibration data, and QC results
  in the lab notebook

## 10. Training Record

Before measuring soil pH and EC independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-L300](SOP-L300-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd) in
   full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Demonstrate pH meter three-point calibration with acceptable slope
4. Demonstrate conductivity meter calibration
5. Prepare 1:1 and 1:5 extracts and measure a set of at least 5
   practice soils under supervision with acceptable duplicate precision
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Example Calculation and Reporting {.appendix}

```{r}
#| label: soil-pH-EC-example
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

library(tidyverse)

# Example data entry
soil_data <- tibble(
  sample_id = c("PV-01", "PV-02", "PV-03", "PV-04", "PV-05"),
  pH_water_1_1 = c(6.82, 7.45, 5.91, 8.12, 7.03),
  pH_CaCl2_1_1 = c(6.48, 7.10, 5.55, 7.78, 6.68),
  EC_1_5_uS_cm = c(245, 1820, 85, 3450, 310),
  texture = c("loam", "clay", "sand", "clay", "loam")
)

# Estimate EC_e from 1:5 EC using texture-based conversion factors
conversion <- c(sand = 7, loam = 9, clay = 11.5)

soil_data <- soil_data %>%
  mutate(
    EC_e_dS_m = (EC_1_5_uS_cm / 1000) * conversion[texture],
    salinity_class = case_when(
      EC_e_dS_m < 2 ~ "Non-saline",
      EC_e_dS_m < 4 ~ "Slightly saline",
      EC_e_dS_m < 8 ~ "Moderately saline",
      EC_e_dS_m < 16 ~ "Strongly saline",
      TRUE ~ "Very strongly saline"
    ),
    pH_class = case_when(
      pH_water_1_1 < 4.5 ~ "Extremely acidic",
      pH_water_1_1 < 5.5 ~ "Strongly acidic",
      pH_water_1_1 < 6.5 ~ "Moderately acidic",
      pH_water_1_1 < 7.5 ~ "Neutral",
      pH_water_1_1 < 8.5 ~ "Moderately alkaline",
      TRUE ~ "Strongly alkaline"
    )
  )

print(soil_data %>% select(sample_id, pH_water_1_1, pH_CaCl2_1_1,
                           EC_e_dS_m, salinity_class, pH_class))
```


## Appendix B: Reagent Preparation {.appendix}

### 0.01 M CaCl~2~ Solution

1. Weigh 1.47 g of CaCl~2~-2H~2~O (MW 147.01) on the analytical
   balance
2. Dissolve in approximately 800 mL of DI water in a 1 L volumetric
   flask
3. Bring to 1 L with DI water and mix thoroughly
4. Label with concentration, preparation date, and preparer's initials
5. Store at room temperature in a capped polyethylene or borosilicate
   bottle. Stable indefinitely.


## Appendix C: Troubleshooting {.appendix}

| Symptom                       | Probable Cause                  | Corrective Action              |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| pH reading drifts continuously | Poorly buffered soil; electrode junction fouled | Allow longer equilibration (up to 5 min); clean electrode per [SOP-L40](SOP-L40-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd) |
| pH in CaCl~2~ higher than pH in water | Measurement error; contaminated CaCl~2~ solution | Verify CaCl~2~ concentration; recalibrate meter; re-measure |
| EC reading unexpectedly high  | Fertilizer residue; saline soil; contaminated beaker | Verify with a blank; use acid-washed glassware ([SOP-L12](SOP-L12-glassware-cleaning.qmd)) |
| EC reading near zero          | Electrode not fully immersed; air bubble in cell | Reposition cell; tap to dislodge bubbles |
| Large difference between 1:1 and 1:5 EC | Normal; dilution effect | Report both with the ratio clearly stated; convert to EC~e~ using appropriate factor |
| pH calibration slope below 90% | Aged electrode; dirty glass bulb | Soak in cleaning solution or 0.1 M HCl for 15--30 min; if slope does not recover, replace electrode |
